source.paraphrase: The App Router declares head data with the metadata export. next/head is the Pages Router component and does not run under app.

invariants.why: next/head belongs to the Pages Router and is valid there; in app/ files the metadata export owns the document head.
invariants.fixHint: Export a metadata object from the page or layout. Keep next/head only in files that still run under the Pages Router.
invariants.avoid: Only the exact next/head literal in an import/export source or first literal require/import argument is forbidden in app paths. next/headers, ordinary text and import option values are allowed. Computed specifiers and aliased runtime loaders are outside this syntax slice.

source.paraphrase: Images go through the Image component so the framework can resize, lazy-load, and serve modern formats per viewport.

invariants.why: A raw img skips resizing and lazy loading, shipping full-weight files and causing layout shift the Image component prevents.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the element with Image from next/image and give it a width, height, or fill plus an alt description.
invariants.avoid: The rule matches a JSX img element, including the open-plus-close form. Markup assembled as a string, including a template returned from a .ts helper, is not an element.

source.paraphrase: Fonts load through next/font so builds self-host the files. Remote stylesheet links reintroduce render-blocking requests and layout shift.

invariants.why: A googleapis link tag moves font loading back to a render-blocking remote request, undoing the self-hosting and shift guarantees.
invariants.fixHint: Load the family with next/font and apply the generated class name or variable. Remove the link tag entirely.
invariants.avoid: The rule matches a JSX link element whose text contains fonts.googleapis.com, including a preconnect to that host. A template string in a .ts helper is not a link element.

source.work: Next.js fetch reference, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch; Migrating to Cache Components, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components
source.locator: options.cache auto no cache; fetch cache options
source.paraphrase: In the previous model, fetch defaults to auto no cache, so a missing cache option is not a violation. With cacheComponents enabled, fetch is uncached unless it runs inside use cache, and cache or next options are not required.

invariants.why: The default is valid in both models. The check stays off. It runs only when Cache Components is not enabled, so a bare fetch inside use cache is not reported as a missing fetch cache option.
invariants.fixHint: In the previous model, pass cache or next.revalidate only when you want an explicit policy. With cacheComponents, cache the function with use cache and cacheLife instead of fetch cache options.
invariants.avoid: An empty options object or an unrelated option such as signal does not declare a policy. The check does not run when the first existing root next.config.js, next.config.mjs, or next.config.ts sets cacheComponents to literal true. A nested experimental.cacheComponents, a comment, or a computed flag does not enable that exception. next.config.mts is not read.

source.work: Next.js App Router API reference, fetch
source.paraphrase: Conflicting cache options such as no-store together with a positive revalidation interval are both ignored.

invariants.why: The developer requested incompatible cache lifetimes, so neither option governs the fetch as expected.
invariants.fixHint: Keep cache: 'no-store' for uncached responses, or remove it and set next.revalidate to a positive interval.
invariants.avoid: Swapping the order of the options does not change their conflict. An unrelated body object is not the fetch options object.

source.work: Next.js API reference, use client, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-client; React reference, use server, https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-server
source.locator: use client usage; use server caveats
source.paraphrase: 'use client' goes at the top of the file, before imports, and cannot be placed inside a function. 'use server' must be at the very beginning of its file or function, above other code (comments are fine), in single or double quotes, not backticks.

invariants.why: A directive anywhere else is an ordinary string. The file silently stays a Server Component, or the function never becomes a Server Action, and hooks or browser APIs then fail at build or run time.
invariants.fixHint: Move the directive to the first line of the file, above every import, in single or double quotes. For an inline Server Action, put 'use server' as the first statement of the async function body.
invariants.avoid: Comments and other quoted string statements before the directive are not flagged. 'use server' as the first statement of a function body is allowed. Strings that merely contain the words, in variables or JSX, are not directives and are not flagged.

source.locator: Metadata object and generateMetadata function, good to know
source.paraphrase: The metadata object and generateMetadata function exports are only supported in Server Components.

invariants.why: Next.js rejects a metadata export from a 'use client' page or layout at build time, so the page loses its title and description or the build fails.
invariants.fixHint: Remove 'use client' from the page or layout and move the interactive part into a child client component. Keep metadata or generateMetadata on the server file.
invariants.avoid: Only exported metadata or generateMetadata in page and layout files under app/ or src/app/ whose leading directive is 'use client' are flagged, including export { x as metadata }. A local metadata constant that is not exported, and server files that mention the directive in a comment, are allowed.

source.work: Next.js API reference, cookies, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies; Next.js 16 upgrade guide, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16
source.locator: cookies good to know; Async Request APIs (breaking change)
source.paraphrase: cookies, headers and draftMode are async and must be awaited or unwrapped with React's use. Next.js 15 kept temporary synchronous access with a warning; Next.js 16 removes it.

invariants.why: On Next.js 16 the call returns a Promise, so .get or .isEnabled reads undefined or throws. Next.js 15 still accepts the synchronous call and logs a deprecation warning.
invariants.fixHint: Await the call first, for example const store = await cookies(); store.get('theme'). In a component that cannot be async, unwrap the Promise with React's use(). https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16
invariants.avoid: Only a member read directly on cookies(), headers() or draftMode() imported from next/headers, including renamed imports, is flagged. Awaited calls, use(...), .then/.catch/.finally and same-named functions from other modules pass. A result stored in a variable first is not traced. The finding is a warning unless the nearest package.json declares next entirely on 16 or newer (including 16 prereleases). Next.js 15, an older release, and a specifier that can still install 15 stay warnings.

source.paraphrase: Next.js 16 removes synchronous access to params and searchParams in page.js. Next.js 15 kept a temporary synchronous compatibility path.

invariants.why: The page props are Promises. Reading .slug or destructuring them without await yields undefined query data instead of the requested page.
invariants.fixHint: Await the prop, then read it: const { slug } = await params and const query = await searchParams. In a Client Component, unwrap the Promise with React's use(). https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16
invariants.avoid: Only page files under app/ or src/app/ are read. A member read, index read, or object destructure of params or searchParams is flagged, and so is props.params.x or props.searchParams.x when that access is not itself awaited. A nested parameter pattern is flagged. A use inside a block that declares a local of the same name, including one from await, use(), useParams(), or useSearchParams(), is not flagged. A parameter read in that same block is not flagged either. The rule runs only when next is declared entirely on 16 or newer.

source.locator: Async Request APIs (Breaking change); Async parameters for icon and open-graph Image
source.paraphrase: params in layout, route, default, opengraph-image, twitter-image, icon, and apple-icon are Promises. generateImageMetadata still receives synchronous params. searchParams is documented for page.js.

invariants.why: A synchronous read of the params Promise drops the dynamic segment, so the layout, route, or image is built for the wrong key.
invariants.fixHint: Await params before reading it: const { slug } = await params. Keep the synchronous read inside generateImageMetadata. https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16
invariants.avoid: Page files are covered by NEXT-PARAMS-001. This rule reads layout, route, default, and the image generator files. A member, index, destructure, or nested parameter pattern named params is flagged. A use inside a block that declares a local named params, including URLSearchParams, is not flagged. A parameter read in that same block is not flagged either. searchParams in a layout is not the page request API and is not flagged. generateImageMetadata is excluded. The rule runs only when next is declared entirely on 16 or newer.

source.paraphrase: The sitemap function receives id as a Promise. generateSitemaps still returns plain ids. The previous code multiplied the id number directly.

invariants.why: Multiplying the Promise produces NaN, so the generated sitemap URLs start at the wrong offset.
invariants.fixHint: Await id, then convert it: const resolved = await id; const start = Number(resolved) * 50000. https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16
invariants.avoid: Only sitemap files under app/ or src/app/ are read. The flagged shape is an identifier named id used in arithmetic, including Number(id) and parentheses. await id passes. A local const that reuses the name id is flagged too. generateSitemaps is excluded. The rule runs only when next is declared entirely on 16 or newer.

source.locator: Async parameters for icon and open-graph Image
source.paraphrase: The image generating function in opengraph-image, twitter-image, icon, and apple-icon receives id as a Promise. generateImageMetadata still receives synchronous params and does not receive this id.

invariants.why: Storing or reading the Promise as if it were the image id string builds the wrong image, or none.
invariants.fixHint: Await id, or unwrap it with React's use() in a Client Component: const imageId = await id. https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16
invariants.avoid: Only opengraph-image, twitter-image, icon, and apple-icon files are read. An identifier named id is flagged when it is stored in a const, read as a member, or indexed, including through parentheses. await id and use(id) pass. A helper that copies an id parameter into a const is flagged too. The rule runs only when next is declared entirely on 16 or newer.

source.work: Next.js 16 upgrade guide, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16; Next.js 16 release, https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16
source.paraphrase: revalidateTag now requires a second argument. The upgrade guide shows a cacheLife profile such as 'max'. The Next.js 16 release also allows an inline { expire: number } object. The single-argument form is deprecated and is a TypeScript error.

invariants.why: A one-argument call no longer typechecks on Next.js 16, so the tag the author meant to refresh is not part of a typed cache profile. Next.js 15 still uses the single-argument form.
invariants.fixHint: Pass a cacheLife profile, usually 'max', or { expire: seconds }: revalidateTag('posts', 'max'). For read-your-writes inside a Server Action, call updateTag(tag) instead. https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16
invariants.avoid: Only a call whose function is revalidateTag imported from next/cache, including a renamed import, is flagged, and only when it has fewer than two arguments and no spread. A profile string, a variable, and { expire: number } all satisfy the second argument. updateTag and a same-named helper from another module pass. The rule runs only when next is declared entirely on 16 or newer.
